item.title: Saudi Arabia to Start Issuing Hajj Visas on Sunday, Four Months Ahead of 2026 Pilgrimage
item.description: The Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah announced the commencement of visa issuance for the 2026 Hajj season (1447 AH) on Sunday, February 8, corresponding to Sha’ban 20. This early launch is part of an accelerated timeline designed to enhance service readiness and ensure the comfort of pilgrims approximately four months ahead of the rituals, in alignment with the Kingdom’s Vision 2030. item.title: Bahrain: USD 500 Domestic Worker Salary Optional, Not Mandatory: Recruitment Offices
item.description: The Bahrain Recruitment Offices Association has clarified that setting a domestic worker’s salary at USD 500 is optional and not a mandatory requirement under current regulations, stressing that any wage increase must be approved by the employer and follow official legal frameworks. item.title: Bahrain: Man Arrested For BD 5,000 Theft From Zinj Medical Centre
item.description: The Capital Governorate Police Directorate has arrested a 39-year-old man for stealing more than BD 5,000 from a medical centre in the Zinj area, the Ministry of Interior confirmed. The directorate stated that upon receiving information about the incident, immediate search and investigation operations were launched, including the collection of evidence. item.title: Bahrain: Debate To Raise Witness Evidence Limit To BD1,000
item.description: Shura Council members will revisit on Sunday a draft change to Bahrain’s evidence law that would double the limit for using witness testimony in civil cases from BD500 to BD1,000. The proposal would amend Decree-Law No. 14 of 1996 on evidence in civil and commercial matters by amending Articles 61 and 62. item.description: The Ministry of Interior has confirmed the arrest of a 29-year-old man accused of targeting a 17-year-old girl through a social networking platform and attempting to exploit her by intimidation and online manipulation. item.title: Kuwait Bans Use Of External Loudspeakers At Mosques During Ramadan
item.description: Kuwait has banned the use of external loudspeakers at mosques during Ramadan, tightening regulations on public religious activities as authorities seek to balance worship practices with public order and neighbourhood considerations. item.title: Oman Mediates Indirect US-Iran Talks Over Tehran’s Nuclear Program
item.description: Oman mediated indirect talks Friday between Iran and the United States over Tehran’s nuclear program, with convoys for the two countries arriving for meetings separately with the sultanate’s top diplomat. There was no immediate comment from either the Iranian or the American sides. Associated Press journalists saw Iranians at a palace on the outskirts of the Omani capital, Muscat, near its international airport.
